name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: We should add a "single-line safe-change" flag to our prompts, which auto-applies only typo fixes and minor documentation edits. This decision prioritizes speed and convenience, allowing us to quickly refine our work without manual review. By accepting this approach, we trade off some control over more substantial changes, which will still require manual review and approval. This trade-off is worthwhile, as it enables us to efficiently refine our prompts and focus on more complex improvements.

name: Gauge
text: The "single-line safe-change" flag still risks missing context shifts, and typos can have broader implications than just a single line. A better alternative might be to implement a more nuanced, multi-step review process that considers the broader context of each edit, rather than relying on arbitrary flags. What would settle this argument is a clear analysis of the types of errors our current review process is missing, and whether a more contextual approach would actually catch more issues without overly slowing down our workflow.
